newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Chevron to invest $350 mln more in Kazakh oil.
newsitem.headline: Chevron to invest $350 mln more in Kazakh oil.

text.p: U.S. oil major Chevron Corp is to invest a further $350 million in its oil joint venture in western Kazakhstan in 1997, a Kazakh official said on Tuesday.

A spokesman for Prime Minister Akezhan Kazhegeldin, widely regarded as the official in charge of foreign oil investment, told a news conference the sum was agreed because of improved conditions for foreign investors. He gave no further details.
Chevron owns 50 percent of the Tengizchevroil joint venture while U.S. Mobil Corp and the Kazakh government each hold 25 percent.

Situated in the desert steppes in the west of the Central Asian nation near the Caspian Sea, the venture's Tengiz oilfield has estimated reserves of 6-9 billion barrels with output projected at 700,000 barrels per day (bpd) by 2010.
The $20 billion venture already produces around 100,000 bpd.
